You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Do you mean total deaths/injuries per battle, per ship, or a list of death records? Below is a useful default query that returns death tolls (killed, injured, total) aggregated by battle. Tell me if you want a different breakdown.

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  b.date,
  b.result,
  COUNT(d.id) AS incident_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) AS total_killed,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.injured), 0) AS total_injured,
  COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0) + COALESCE(d.injured, 0)), 0) AS total_casualties
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date, b.result
ORDER BY total_casualties DESC;
```
I want to make sure the death toll is looked at for each specific event or instance.

Here's a query that returns one row per death event (each record in the death table) with ship and battle context and the per-event killed/injured/total counts:

```sql
SELECT
  d.id AS event_id,
  d.note,
  COALESCE(d.killed, 0) AS killed,
  COALESCE(d.injured, 0) AS injured,
  COALESCE(d.killed, 0) + COALESCE(d.injured, 0) AS total_casualties,
  s.id AS ship_id,
  s.name AS ship_name,
  s.ship_type,
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  b.date AS battle_date,
  b.result AS battle_result
FROM death d
LEFT JOIN ship s ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN battle b ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
ORDER BY b.id, d.id;
```
I want to also get the minimum death toll recorded for any instance.

Do you mean the minimum total casualties (killed + injured) per death event? The query below returns one row per death event and includes a column showing the minimum total casualties observed across all events.

```sql
SELECT
  d.id AS event_id,
  d.note,
  COALESCE(d.killed, 0) AS killed,
  COALESCE(d.injured, 0) AS injured,
  COALESCE(d.killed, 0) + COALESCE(d.injured, 0) AS total_casualties,
  (SELECT MIN(COALESCE(killed, 0) + COALESCE(injured, 0)) FROM death) AS min_total_casualties_any_instance,
  s.id AS ship_id,
  s.name AS ship_name,
  s.ship_type,
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  b.date AS battle_date,
  b.result AS battle_result
FROM death d
LEFT JOIN ship s ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN battle b ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
ORDER BY b.id, d.id;
```
also want to get the max death toll recorded for any instance.

```sql
SELECT
  d.id AS event_id,
  d.note,
  COALESCE(d.killed, 0) AS killed,
  COALESCE(d.injured, 0) AS injured,
  COALESCE(d.killed, 0) + COALESCE(d.injured, 0) AS total_casualties,
  (SELECT MIN(COALESCE(killed, 0) + COALESCE(injured, 0)) FROM death) AS min_total_casualties_any_instance,
  (SELECT MAX(COALESCE(killed, 0) + COALESCE(injured, 0)) FROM death) AS max_total_casualties_any_instance,
  s.id AS ship_id,
  s.name AS ship_name,
  s.ship_type,
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  b.date AS battle_date,
  b.result AS battle_result
FROM death d
LEFT JOIN ship s ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN battle b ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
ORDER BY b.id, d.id;
```
